page.layout: One page of verse, one column, set in lines with indents; running head at top; page number at top left. No margin notes on this page. A right-margin fragment "AD" at the lower right belongs to the next page's catchword position and is not printed text of this page's block; it is recorded as a catchword.

main_text.p:
Salue venusta& nitidum decus
Anni recurrens perpetua vice,
Et flos renascentis iuuentae
Infenium properantis aui.

Cum blanda veris temperies nouo
Illuxit orbi, primaque secula
Fluxere fluenti metallo
Sponte sua sine lege iusta:

Talis per omnes continuus decor
Annos tepenti rura Fauonio
Mulcebat & nullis feraces
Seminibus recreabat agros.

Talis beatus incubat insulis
Felicis aurae perpetuus tepor,
Et nescius campis senectae
Difficilis querulique morbi.

Talis silentum per tacitum nemus
Leni susurrat murmure spiritus,
Lethenque iuxta obliuiosam
Funereas agitat cupressos.

Forsan supremis cum Deus ignibus
Piabit orbem, laetaque secula
Mundo reducet, talis aura
Aethereas animas fouebit.

Salue fugacis gloria seculi.
Salue secunda digna dies nota.
Salue vetustae vitae imago,
Et specimen venientis aui.

page.notes: Verse set as stanzas with lines indented; the last lines of the page are in the same type. The word "AD" at the lower right is a catchword-like fragment printed beside the text and is recorded as catchword. Long s rendered as plain s. The first stanza has a printed "&" for "et". Italic/roman distinctions are not visible in the scan; the text is roman throughout. Doubtful: "Talis" in the first line of stanza four and "Piabit" in stanza six are given as printed; "Infenium" and "Illuxit" are as printed (no correction made). Lines 1–4 of the first stanza show no reference marks.
